summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for placement of a Dobhoff feeding tube and replacement of his tunneled central line due to malnutrition and ongoing treprostinil therapy for portopulmonary hypertension. He reported significant anorexia and weight loss attributed to treprostinil, despite using megestrol to improve appetite. A tunneled line was successfully placed on hospital day two, and a Dobhoff tube was inserted endoscopically the following day, with radiographic confirmation of correct placement. Tube feeds were initiated and tolerated well. Five liters of ascitic fluid were removed during paracentesis, with no signs of infection. His kidney function improved, with creatinine normalizing, and liver enzymes remained stable. He was discharged home with services to continue tube feeds, treprostinil via the new line, and all home medications, including ciprofloxacin for SBP prophylaxis. Outpatient follow-up and lab monitoring were arranged.
